en: Theragāthā 3.15 Tikanipāta, Paṭhamavagga The Elder Sāriputta I am one who has reached the goal, one whose burden is laid down, who has lived the holy life; there is nothing more for me to do. I have cut off craving at its root, like a palm tree with its top cut off; I am free from birth, I have transcended all suffering. I am one who has reached the goal, one whose burden is laid down, who has lived the holy life; there is nothing more for me to do. I have cut off craving at its root, like a palm tree with its top cut off; I am free from birth, I have transcended all suffering.
The Verses of the Elder Hārita:
“He who desires to do later what ought to have been done earlier;”
He falls from that state of happiness and later regrets it; for what one should do,
One should not say what one would not do;
the wise discern the person who speaks without acting.
taught by the Perfectly Enlightened One—
“Where suffering ceases,” said the Elder Hārita.
